::: {#thm-directed-degrees}
#### Degrees in a directed graph

For every directed graph $G = (V, E)$ (@def-directed-graph),

$$
\sum_{v \in V} \deg^+(v) = \card{E} = \sum_{v \in V} \deg^-(v),
$$

where $\deg^+$ is the out-degree (@def-out-degree) and $\deg^-$ is the in-degree (@def-in-degree).

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

Each edge starts at exactly one vertex,
so sorting the edges by the vertex where they start puts each edge in exactly one group.
The group of $v$ has $\deg^+(v)$ edges,
so the sizes of the groups add up to $\sum_{v \in V} \deg^+(v) = \card{E}$.
Sorting the edges by the vertex where they end gives $\sum_{v \in V} \deg^-(v) = \card{E}$ in the same way.

:::

:::
